title: League of Lezhë
capsule: The League of Lezhë, founded on 2 March 1444 in the Albanian coastal town of Lezhë, was a military alliance of Albanian noble houses — Kastrioti, Arianiti, Muzaka, Thopia, Zaharia, Balsha, and Crnojević — united under Gjergj Kastrioti (Skanderbeg), who took the title Dominus Albaniae. Fielding roughly 8,000 warriors, the League defeated Ottoman forces repeatedly over 24 years, including the major battles of Torvioll (1444) and Albulena (1457). After Skanderbeg's death at Lezhë on 17 January 1468, Lekë III Dukagjini led continued resistance until the Ottoman capture of Shkodra in 1479 effectively extinguished organized Albanian opposition.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political extent of the League is reasonably documented in Venetian and Ottoman sources, but its territorial control was fluid — it functioned primarily as a military coalition rather than an administered state, making polygon boundaries speculative.
